summary: 100-foot Aermotor LS-40 fire tower in Okeechobee County, Florida; NHLR-registered 2016; cab rehabilitated 2009. A WPTV report describes drought-season ranger watches from the tower.

facts.agency: Florida Department of Agriculture & Consumer Services

events.note: Registered July 24, 2016 as US 1066, FL 13; nominated by Robert Spear

evidence.supports: design: 100-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower with 15 landings
evidence.quote: This 100' Aermotor LS-40 tower features 15 landings.
Its observation cab was rehabilitated in 2009.
Florida Department of Agriculture & Consumer Services

evidence.supports: served as a lookout for 50 years (as reported)
evidence.quote: For 50 years, the Okeechobee County fire watch tower has served as a lookout for firefighters spotting brush fires.

evidence.supports: 81 steps and nine flights of stairs
evidence.quote: 81 steps and 9 flights of stairs to the top of the fire watch tower
Up top firefighters have a viewpoint reaching 30 miles.

evidence.supports: Florida Forest Service ranger Robert Smith
evidence.quote: said Ranger Robert Smith, Florida Forest Service in Okeechobee.

evidence.supports: up to eight hours in the tower during severe drought
evidence.quote: In severe drought, Ranger Smith spends up to 8 hours in the tower.

evidence.supports: fire finder used to pinpoint a fire
evidence.quote: Using a fire finder they can pinpoint exactly where a fire is.

sources.title: Okeechobee fire watch tower helps spot wildfires

notes_for_editor: The WPTV report carries no date in the copy read, so its 50-year figure and the drought-season staffing read are undated. Staffing is coded 'emergency', the closest schema value, for the severe-drought watch described; the report gives no schedule for other seasons. The Register and the report use different agency names (FDACS and Florida Forest Service); neither source says how they relate, so both are reported as written. No build date found. Access is omitted: neither source describes public visits.
